newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis daughters describe shares dispute.
newsitem.headline: Publicis daughters describe shares dispute.

text.p: Two daughters of Publicis founder Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet have aired their views to Publicis shareholders on plans by one of them, Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, to sell her 20-percent stake in Publicis.
The sisters said at the Publicis annual meeting on Friday that they agreed on the need to maintain family control of the group. The family currently owns 60 percent of Publicis.

Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, the founder's youngest daughter, told the meeting she "did not agree with the structure of Somarel," the Publicis holding company. It was unfair because it prevented her from selling her stake with complete freedom, she said.

Elisabeth Badinter, chairman of Somarel and the second daughter of Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet, who died just over a year ago, said her sister's sale of her stake was "for the moment quite complex given the structure of Somarel and the sales conditions" it imposed.
Michele Bleustein-Blanchet owns a third of Somarel, which itself has 38.4 percent of Publicis shares and 45 percent of its voting rights. She also owns seven percent of Publicis directly.
Her holding, which amounts to some 20 percent, is valued at nearly a 1.0 billion francs ($170.6 million). DT/SLA ($ = 5.861 French Francs)
